subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

Statement 1: The magnetic field lines produced around a straight current-carrying conductor form concentric circles centred along the wire.

Statement 2: The direction of these magnetic field lines can be determined using the right-hand thumb rule.

options.text: Statement 1 is incorrect, but 2 is correct.
Statement 1 is correct, but 2 is incorrect.

solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The magnetic field lines produced around a straight current-carrying conductor form concentric circles centered along the wire.

 
 
• When an electric current flows through a straight conductor, such as a wire, it generates a magnetic field around it.
 
• The pattern of this magnetic field consists of **concentric circles** centered on the wire.
 
• This phenomenon is explained by the **Oersted experiment**, which demonstrated the relationship between electricity and magnetism.
 
• *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** The direction of these magnetic field lines can be determined using the right-hand thumb rule.
 
 
• The **right-hand thumb rule** states that if you hold a straight current-carrying conductor in your right hand, with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current, the curled fingers of your hand indicate the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• This rule is crucial for determining the orientation of the magnetic field produced around conductors.
 
• It aligns with the principles of electromagnetism and is widely used in practical applications.
 
• *Hence, Statement 2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• Both statements explain essential aspects of the magnetic field generated by a current-carrying conductor and are **scientifically accurate.**
 
• ***Thus, the correct answer is: Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnetic Field Lines:**

 
 
• Magnetic field lines are **invisible lines** that represent the magnetic field around a magnet or a current-carrying conductor.
 
• They are **continuous loops** that emerge from the north pole of a magnet and re-enter at the south pole.
 
• The density of magnetic field lines indicates the **strength of the magnetic field**; closer lines signify a stronger field.
 
 
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is a part of the broader set of rules in electromagnetism to determine the direction of magnetic fields.
 
• It is applicable to both straight conductors and circular loops of current.
 
• The rule is intuitive and forms the basis for understanding the behavior of magnetic fields in various devices like solenoids and motors.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Magnetic Fields:**
 
 
• The principles of magnetic fields are applied in designing **electromagnets**, electric motors, transformers, and generators.
 
• Magnetic field mapping is used in medical imaging technologies like **Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI).**
 
• It also plays a critical role in navigation systems and magnetometers.
 
 
 
• **Oersted's Experiment:**
 
 
• In 1820, **Hans Christian Oersted** discovered that a magnetic field is created around a conductor carrying electric current.
 
• This experiment laid the foundation for the field of electromagnetism, connecting electricity and magnetism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnetic Field Strength:** The strength of the magnetic field around a straight conductor decreases as the distance from the conductor increases.
 
• **Magnetic Compass:** A magnetic compass can be used to visualize the direction of the magnetic field lines around a current-carrying conductor.
 
• **Solenoid:** A solenoid is a coil of wire that generates a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet when current flows through it, demonstrating the same principles of field lines and direction.
 
• **Electromagnetic Devices:** Understanding magnetic field principles is essential for the functioning of devices like electric bells, relays, and magnetic locks.
